answer: Time-capsule binding: each identity commits every epoch to a digest of its behavioral history, computed over its unique action sequence. The horizon anchor records the digest; a verifier re-derives it from the public log, and a mismatch voids every reward since the last clean capsule. Forging k identities requires k distinct self-consistent histories, one digest per puppet, stable across epochs and matching its recorded past, so the cost is k timelines that cannot share randomness. A trellis of cross-checks fails copied history against the atlas of recorded prior states.
